Share security docs (SOC2/ISO) and network checklist
Run baseline benchmark within 2 weeks and share results
Confirm exec readout date for mid-December
action_items: Lina Chen: send POC proposal and pricing (due 2025-12-02)
Marcus Patel: prepare benchmark script, example prompts, and baseline dataset (due 2025-12-05)

summary: AE + SE met with Tempest AI to scope a 6-week POC focused on latency and cost baselining for a real-time summarization workflow. Agreed milestones: kickoff and access provisioning next week, baseline benchmark run in week 2, midpoint performance review with quantitative metrics, and exec readout in mid-December. Security and network requirements to be reviewed; Redwood to share SOC2 + network checklist.
transcript:
Date: 2025-11-29 15:00 UTC | Duration: 40 minutes | Attendees: Lina Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (Head of ML, Tempest AI), Ethan Kline (Platform Eng), Priya Rao (CTO)

00:00 - Lina Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this to 40 minutes, quick intros and then dive into the POC scope and timeline
00:35 - Sofia Martinez: thanks Lina, hi all, Sofia here, we run the ML infra and models team at Tempest, currently evaluating inference platforms for our real-time summarization product
00:55 - Marcus Patel: great, Marcus from Redwood, I'll lead the technical bits - benchmarks, access, and the scripts we use for latency/cost baselining
01:10 - Priya Rao: hi, Priya here, i'm mostly here to make sure the timeline and compliance lines up with our Q4 roadmap
01:28 - Ethan Kline: Ethan, platform, i'll handle creds and network setup with you if we move ahead
01:40 - Lina Chen: perfect, quick qualification: existing stack? where's the model hosted, and do you already have a preferred open model?
01:58 - Sofia Martinez: currently model artifacts live in ECR and we run training on k8s clusters; for inference we have a small in-house endpoint running a quantized Llama 2 variant but cost and tail latency are issues at scale
02:20 - Marcus Patel: ok, so goals are to improve unit cost and get predictable p99 latency under 250ms for 512-token avg requests?
02:36 - Sofia Martinez: yes that's the target, and we want to validate both hosted vs dedicated options - likely dedicated if the latency/cost numbers are favorable and security checks pass
02:50 - Priya Rao: also important: audit logs, SSO (SAML), and KMS integration - we can't ship customer data without those in place
03:05 - Lina Chen: noted. For success criteria we typically codify: p50/p95/p99 latency targets, token cost target (per-1k tokens), and functional parity on quality (ROUGE/abstractive coherence on a small eval set)
03:25 - Marcus Patel: we'll prepare a benchmark harness that does: 1) throughput and latency with realistic sequence length distribution, 2) cost per token using Redwood Optimize settings, 3) quality regression tests on your eval prompts
03:45 - Ethan Kline: how much access do you need? Can we restrict to a temp S3 bucket and a VPC peering or do you need broader infra access?
04:05 - Marcus Patel: temp S3 with sample dataset + either short-lived creds or an object presign flow should be sufficient for the baseline. For dedicated validation we'd need network (VPC) connectivity for full end-to-end tests
04:25 - Sofia Martinez: timeline wise we're aiming for an exec readout mid-December - so roughly 6 weeks, is that doable?
04:40 - Lina Chen: yes, we usually do 4-6 week POCs. Proposed milestones: 1) Kickoff & access setup (week 0), 2) Baseline benchmark & config tuning (week 1-2), 3) Midpoint review with results and pass/fail check (week 3), 4) Extended run for throughput and edge-case checks (week 4), 5) Exec readout (week 5-6)
05:05 - Priya Rao: can you be explicit about deliverables at each milestone? executives will want concrete artifacts
05:18 - Lina Chen: absolutely - kickoff: SOW + runbook + security checklist; baseline: raw benchmark outputs and config used; midpoint: summarized metrics (latency distribution, cost per 1k tokens, quality regressions) and recommended next steps; final: exec slide deck and ops checklist for handoff
05:40 - Marcus Patel: note on benchmarks - we'll run both hosted and a small dedicated cluster, use continuous batching and prefix/KV cache enabled for the workload to simulate real env. (sometimes transcript reads KV cash)
06:05 - Ethan Kline: slight concern on data residency - some of our documents are EU-only, can Redwood support region pinning for the POC?
06:20 - Lina Chen: yes, we have regional routing and can pin to eu-west by policy; for Dedicated we'd provision instances in the region requested
06:35 - Sofia Martinez: security docs - do you have SOC2 and an overview of KMS integration?
06:46 - Lina Chen: we'll send SOC2 report and a KMS integration doc; for VPC/on-prem we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations as well
07:00 - Priya Rao: next on the checklist: what are the failure modes you'd surface in the midpoint review?
07:12 - Marcus Patel: typical failure modes: quality regressions versus your eval set, p99 spikes due to cold KV cache or poor batching, and cost outliers caused by long tail requests. We'll instrument token-level breakdowns so you can correlate cost vs latency per route
07:35 - Ethan Kline: about the benchmark harness - will you share the scripts so we can run internally too?
07:45 - Marcus Patel: yes we'll share the harness and the dockerized runner; goal is reproducibility, so you'll be able to run the same script in your env and our hosted environment
08:10 - Sofia Martinez: on success criteria - we need a hard threshold for cost improvement to justify dedicated: at least 30% reduction in tokens cost vs our current infra assuming similar quality
08:28 - Lina Chen: that sounds reasonable. We'll target that and provide a clear delta calculation in the baseline report
08:40 - Priya Rao: who needs to be involved from Redwood for the kickoff and the midpoint?
08:50 - Lina Chen: kickoff: AE + SE (Marcus) + Solutions eng if needed; midpoint: SE-led deep dive plus AE and an executive sponsor for readout if we hit the targets
09:05 - Ethan Kline: can we get a quick list of network requirements? firewall rules, port ranges, IP CIDR?
09:16 - Marcus Patel: yes - minimal: outbound to Redwood control plane for telemetry (HTTPS), for Dedicated VPC we need specific peering and healthcheck ports - we'll send a network checklist PDF
09:30 - Sofia Martinez: ok, logistics - let's lock dates: kickoff next Tuesday (2025-12-02) morning for us, midpoint review week of 2025-12-15, exec readout week of 2025-12-22 is that tight?
09:50 - Lina Chen: kickoff 2025-12-02 works; midpoint earlier in the week of 12-15, exec readout I'd suggest try for 12-19 to avoid holiday week, but we'll be flexible with your calendar
10:10 - Priya Rao: can Redwood run a short perf test in our staging environment as part of week 1? we want to see baseline p95/p99 before you tune configs
10:25 - Marcus Patel: yes, staging run is helpful - we'll coordinate with Ethan on creds and run the harness with the same load profile you run in production (or a scaled-down version)
10:45 - Ethan Kline: i'll prepare a temp s3 bucket and a service account with limited permissions, and i'll reach out after the call with the details
11:00 - Lina Chen: perfect. i'll follow up with the SOW, runbook, and a checklist for the network and security docs. Marcus will share the benchmark harness and initial prompt set by end of week
11:20 - Sofia Martinez: just flagging budget approvals - we'll need an internal approval for dedicated if the pilot looks good; who on Redwood handles pricing for reserved capacity?
11:35 - Lina Chen: pricing and committed capacity is handled by AE and Solutions Pricing - i'll include a preliminary pricing sheet in the follow-up, and we can iterate based on the baseline numbers
11:50 - Marcus Patel: technical note: for fairness in the benchmark we'll keep model weights identical and only vary serving infra and batching/quantization profiles - avoid changing the model itself mid-POC
12:10 - Priya Rao: good. last question: are there any known gotchas with long-context workloads and KV cache behavior?
12:22 - Marcus Patel: yes - for long-contexts we pay attention to KV cache warmup and memory pressure on smaller GPU instances; we recommend monitoring KV hit rate and include a warmup phase in the harness
12:41 - Ethan Kline: ok thanks, that helps.
12:50 - Lina Chen: recap and next steps: 1) Lina to send SOW + pricing + security docs (due 2025-12-02), 2) Ethan to send access (due 2025-12-01), 3) Marcus to deliver benchmark harness and prompts (due 2025-12-05), 4) schedule kickoff 2025-12-02 and midpoint week of 12-15, exec readout target week of 12-19
13:15 - Sofia Martinez: thanks all, we'll review the docs and confirm kickoff attendees
13:25 - Priya Rao: thanks everyone, looking forward to it
13:30 - Lina Chen: thanks team, we'll follow up in email with the links to docs and the network checklist

Notes: references to shared artifacts: SOW draft (link to drive: https://redwood.app/sow-tempest-draft), benchmark harness repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-bench), network checklist (attached in follow-up). Some transcript mis-words observed (e.g., KV cash vs KV cache).

Action Items (recap):
- Lina Chen: send POC proposal, SOW, pricing sheet and security docs (SOC2) by 2025-12-02
- Ethan Kline: provide temp S3 creds / bucket and staging access by 2025-12-01
- Marcus Patel: share benchmark harness, docker runner, and sample prompts by 2025-12-05
- Priya Rao: confirm exec readout date and attendees by 2025-12-08

End of transcript.
